title: The Chicken and Egg of Commitment and Trust
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This short post treats trust and commitment as a chicken-and-egg pair that feed each other in a team. Admired Leadership starts with the familiar claim that people who trust a leader become more committed, then adds that neuroscience research shows the reverse also holds: committing to a leader and vision raises trust. Since nobody can say which comes first, the author asks whether leaders should invest in trust to win commitment or push commitment to earn trust. The answer offered is that good leaders do both, while the best leaders emphasize each deliberately, building trust in relationships and promoting commitment to the vision. The payoff described is team members who focus, engage, bounce back from setbacks and behave more consistently.
points: Trust and commitment reinforce one another, so progress on either raises the other.
The post distinguishes two leadership levers: relationship-building to earn trust and vision-building to earn commitment.
Leaders are advised to cultivate both deliberately rather than assume one will follow automatically.
Trusting, committed team members are described as more focused, resilient and consistent.
quotes: When team members commit to the leader and the organization’s vision, they amplify their trust in both. When we trust, we elevate our commitment. When we commit, we expand our trust.

The chicken and egg dynamic of trust and commitment is important for leaders because they require different actions. Should a leader invest in building trust to garner commitment, or should they focus their attention on gaining commitment to foster trust?

They build trust in their relationships and then reap the benefit of higher commitment to themselves and the team. They promote commitment to the enterprise and its vision within the team and enjoy more trust in their relationships as a result. What a bargain!

Good leaders know that team members who trust them and are loyal to the team go above and beyond to lift themselves and others toward sustainable success. They focus their attention more easily, engage more passionately, overcome setbacks and challenges more comfortably, and behave more consistently.

That’s why savvy leaders do their best to amplify the trust individual team members feel toward them while also deepening the commitment they have to the team and its vision. When leaders get this emphasis right, they create a delicious meal with both the chicken and the egg.
